## Findings 2026-10-28 20:05–20:40 PDT

**The plateau metric is not process RSS.** `infra/scripts/observability.sh` publishes `docker stats` MemUsage as `container_memory_rss_bytes` / `memory_rss_bytes`, parsed from Docker's rounded display string, so "2.5GiB" logs as exactly 2,684,354,560. On cgroup v2 that figure is the container's memory charge minus inactive file cache, so it includes active page cache. The metric name overstates what it measures, and its 2–3 significant figures hide small changes.

**But this time the memory was the process's own.** Sampling the new container's cgroup `memory.stat` every 5 minutes after the 20:16 PDT redeploy:

| PDT | docker usage | anon | active+inactive file | process RSS |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 20:17 | 64 MiB | 60.5 MB | 35 MB | 75 MB |
| 20:22 | 733 MiB | 544 MB | 147 MB | 561 MB |
| 20:27 | 773 MiB | 583 MB | 141 MB | 599 MB |
| 20:32 | 794 MiB | 583 MB | 171 MB | 600 MB |
| 20:37 | — | 583 MB | — | — |

The only work between 20:17 and 20:22 was one completion-verify gate job (keepalive log: precheck 20:21:39, search_files tool call 20:22:05, verify step complete 20:22:42 after 56 s). The job finished, 3 threads remain, and 583 MB of anonymous memory stayed resident afterwards. By contrast, 9 concurrent `next_batch` calls in the same image return their memory when they finish (see teenage-unquieted-ringworm).

**Not import cost.** In the same image, importing `rebar.mcp_server`, the completion and plan-review gate modules, `boto3` and `anthropic` brings RSS to 73 MB.

**Ruled out by reading:** both pinned-ticket-view owners close their view (`close_precheck._completion_precheck` in a `finally`, `completion.verify_completion` via `owns_ticket_view`).

**Next:** run the completion gate 3 times in one process inside the MCP image against an isolated store clone, recording RSS after each run, to tell a per-run leak (grows each time) from a one-time cache (one step, then flat).

comments.body:
## Local gate loop (MCP image, Linux, isolated store clone), 2026-10-28 ~20:50 PDT

`rebar.llm.completion.verify_completion` called 3 times in one process. The model step did not run: the provider call failed with an Anthropic "Could not resolve authentication method" (the frontier class's `anthropic:` fallback), so the run covers precheck, pinned ticket view, store reads and tool setup, not the model turn.

| | RSS after (gc.collect) | GATE_PEAK_RSS delta |
|---|---|---|
| start | 36 MB | |
| run 1 | 385 MB | +231 MB |
| run 2 | 377 MB | +4.5 MB |
| run 3 | 392 MB | +3.6 MB |

So the non-model part of the gate retains about 350 MB after the first run and then stays flat. That is a one-time cost, not a per-run leak. It matches the first step on the box (60 MB → 544 MB after one job) to within the model-turn portion, which this run did not cover.

Still unexplained: the old container's stepwise climb to 2.68 GB (18:03–18:43 PDT) and the earlier 3.2 GB plateau. Hypotheses: (a) high-water retention, where concurrent gate jobs and reads each raise the peak and glibc keeps the freed pages; (b) a per-run leak in the model turn, which this run did not exercise. Next: watch the live container through its next gate jobs, recording anon memory against each job's start and end.

## Root cause found 2026-11-16 (PST 11:05-12:15)

Status of related tickets: short-elderly-cock (reconnect window) and teenage-unquieted-ringworm (parallel-call OOM) are both closed `preexisting`; neither changed allocator behaviour, and the plateau reproduces on deployed `b4e0d01b649`.

**Live (read-only SSM), `rebar-mcp-b4e0d01b6491-8092`:** idle at 342 MB 15:38-18:55 UTC; plan-review jobs 19:01-19:44 UTC; then 6 samples 19:47-20:11 UTC all `anon=1273MB`, `RssAnon=1273MB`, 4 threads, 0 calls. PID 1 is the only process. smaps: 703 MB in 11 glibc thread-arena heaps, 547 MB other anon, 22 MB `[heap]`. cgroup `memory.peak` since start 3.04 GB, `oom 0`.

**Local, MCP base image (`python:3.12-slim`), isolated store clone, no model credentials:**
- 6 concurrent store reads: peak 656 MB, idle 71 MB (released).
- Gate-shaped synthetic worker thread (~1 GB of large strings dropped, 1,200 small survivors): idle RssAnon 983 MB, `mallinfo2` free 970 MB; `malloc_trim(0)` -> 24 MB in 70 ms. Reproduces the hold.
- `verify_completion` x2 with a stubbed `TestModel` (no Bedrock): 65 -> 115 -> 127 MB; trim -> 119 MB. The stub path allocates little, so it does not reproduce the full gate footprint; the live model turn's prompts/tool output are the large allocations.
- Separate small growth seen: ~115k Python blocks per gate run (botocore service-model `OrderedDict`s, ~18k per run). Not the plateau (tens of MB, not GB); not addressed here.

**Fix:** `malloc_trim(0)` when the in-flight gauge returns to zero (commit `dd483029d2d`, pending review). New test fails without it ("idle process kept 252 MiB") and passes with it, on Linux.

**Unverified until deploy:** what share of the live 1,273 MB is free-but-held (trimmable) versus live objects; the post-deploy AC records it.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

The on-box MCP container keeps 1.2-2.3 GB of anonymous memory for hours after gate jobs finish, with no request in flight. On 2026-10-28 that plateau sat at 3.2-3.4 GB for 2 h 12 min before a burst of concurrent reads pushed it over the 3.63 GiB limit and the kernel OOM-killed the server (teenage-unquieted-ringworm). It still happens on current main.

## Observation

- 2026-10-28: 0.93 GB -> 3.28 GB between 15:29 and 15:34 PDT with only `PingRequest` in the log; OOM kill at 17:47 PDT.
- 2026-11-16, deployed `b4e0d01b649` (`rebar-mcp-b4e0d01b6491-8092`, read-only SSM): last gate activity 19:44:14 UTC (plan-review jobs, `GATE_PEAK_RSS` up to 1.47 GB). Samples at 19:47, 19:52, 19:57, 20:02, 20:07 and 20:11 UTC all read cgroup `anon=1273MB`, process `RssAnon=1273MB`, 4 threads, 0 `CallToolRequest` in the prior 5 min. Before the gates (15:38-18:55 UTC) the same container idled at 342 MB.
- The holder is PID 1, `/app/.venv/bin/rebar-mcp`, the only process in the container; its `RssAnon` equals the cgroup `anon` figure.
- `/proc/1/smaps` while idle: 703 MB of RSS sits in 11 glibc per-thread arena heaps (64 MB VMAs), 547 MB in other anonymous mappings, 22 MB in the main `[heap]`.
- Store-wide reads return their memory (6 concurrent `list_tickets`/`ready`/`summary` in the MCP image: peak 656 MB, 71 MB idle after).

## Root cause (reproduced)

A gate runs on a worker thread (`spawn_context_daemon`, `src/rebar/_opcert_binding.py:101`; AnyIO workers for the sync tools). Its large strings (prompts, tool output; anything over 512 bytes bypasses pymalloc) come from that thread's glibc arena. When they are freed, glibc keeps the pages in the arena because a few small surviving allocations pin it, and nothing ever calls `malloc_trim`. Reproduced in `python:3.12-slim` (the MCP base image): a gate-shaped worker thread that builds and drops ~1 GB of strings while keeping 1,200 small results leaves RssAnon at 983 MB idle with 970 MB reported free by `mallinfo2`; `malloc_trim(0)` brings it to 24 MB in 70 ms.

## Approach

Return freed C-heap pages to the OS whenever the server goes idle. The in-flight gauge (`InFlightGauge`, `src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:75`) already counts every certified/signing tool call (`admit`, line 122; `track`, line 149), every daemon spawned while serving (`serving_gauge` -> `tracked_work(gauge.hold)`, line 221; `spawn_context_daemon` takes the hold at `_opcert_binding.py:124`), the boot sweep (line 381) and each idle-sync tick (line 437). All of them release through `InFlightGauge._releaser` (line 136). When a release takes the count to zero, call a new `release_freed_heap()` that invokes glibc `malloc_trim(0)` through `ctypes`, outside the gauge lock. Where the C library has no `malloc_trim` (macOS, musl) it is a no-op returning `False`. No config key, environment variable or flag: the behaviour is unconditional, and `malloc_trim(0)` only releases free pages, never live objects.

Rejected: `MALLOC_ARENA_MAX` in `Dockerfile.mcp` (adds an environment knob and only narrows fragmentation); switching allocator (new dependency).

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_mcp_health.py`: add `_malloc_trim()` (cached `ctypes` lookup) and `release_freed_heap()`; `_releaser` calls it when the count reaches zero.
- `tests/unit/test_mcp_idle_heap_release.py` (new): gauge-trigger tests plus a Linux memory test.

## Testing

- Trim fires only on the release that takes the gauge to zero (two holders: none after the first release, one after the second, none on a repeated release); a tracked certified call trims on exit; an uncounted tool (`show_ticket`) never trims.
- `release_freed_heap()` returns `True` on Linux and `False` elsewhere.
- Linux only: a counted worker thread builds and drops ~250 MB of strings while keeping 240 small objects; after the last release, `RssAnon` must be within 64 MiB of the baseline. Measured in the MCP base image: passes with the change; with the trim call removed it fails ("idle process kept 252 MiB").

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The process or thread holding the memory during a plateau is identified with evidence and recorded here: PID 1 `rebar-mcp`, glibc per-thread arenas (Observation above).
- [ ] The holder releases its memory when its work ends: `InFlightGauge._releaser` calls `release_freed_heap()` when the count reaches zero, and `pytest tests/unit/test_mcp_idle_heap_release.py` passes.
- [ ] A test fails if a finished background job keeps its memory: `test_finished_background_job_does_not_keep_its_memory` fails with the trim call removed and passes with it (Linux, CI `ubuntu-latest`).
- [ ] `make verify` passes, and `python scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --check` exits 0.
- [ ] After the change deploys, an idle sample of the live MCP container at least 10 minutes after its last gate job is recorded on this ticket (cgroup `anon` and `/proc/1` `RssAnon`), with the share of memory still held in glibc thread arenas.

file_impact.reason: release freed C-heap pages (malloc_trim) when the in-flight gauge returns to zero
regression tests: trim trigger and Linux idle-memory check
